<hypothesis>
**Hypothesis discrimination**: The critical distinction is whether product (P) affects catalyst activity. Mechanisms with product inhibition (M12, M14, M17) will show reduced rates at higher [P], while substrate-driven inactivation (M9, M11, M16) will not. Dimerization (M2) and dual inactivation (M20) may show intermediate behavior.

**Discriminative experiment design**: Add moderate initial [P] (0.25) with [S]=1.0 and [cat]=0.2. This tests if product presence alters the rate, which would support mechanisms where P interacts with the catalyst (M12, M14, M17) versus those where inactivation is independent of P.

**Contrastive prediction**: 
- **M12/M14/M17** (product-dependent inactivation): Initial rate will be significantly lower due to P binding/inactivating catalyst, with possible biphasic kinetics as P accumulates. 
- **M9/M11/M16** (substrate-driven inactivation): Initial rate will not be affected by [P], showing a sharp decline over time as catalyst becomes inactive. 
- **M20** (catalyst auto-inactivation): Rate decline will be similar to previous runs, unaffected by [P]. 
- **M2** (dimerization): Rate will decrease due to catalyst dimerization, but not as sharply as inactivation mechanisms.
</hypothesis>
